title: Centromeres evolve progressively through selection at the kinetochore interface
authors: Helsen J; Ramachandran K; Sherlock GJ; Dey G
one_liner_zh: 该文研究着丝粒DNA与动粒复合物的进化选择，虽涉及蛋白质-DNA互作但聚焦进化动态而非结合机制建模，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: During mitosis, stable but dynamic interactions between the centromere DNA and kinetochore complex enable accurate and efficient chromosome segregation. Even though many proteins of the kinetochore are highly conserved, centromeres are among the fastest evolving regions within a genome, showing extensive variation even on short evolutionary timescales. Here, we sought to understand how new types of centromeres emerge and reach fixation by mapping centromere evolution across 138 budding yeast species and over 2,500 natural strain isolates. We show that new centromeres spread progressively via drift and subsequent selection, and that the kinetochore interface, which is evolving slowly in relative terms, determines which new centromere variants are tolerated. Together, our findings provide insight into the evolutionary constraints and trajectories shaping centromere evolution.
abstract_zh: 在有丝分裂过程中，着丝粒DNA与动粒复合体之间稳定而动态的相互作用确保了染色体准确且高效地分离。尽管动粒的许多蛋白质高度保守，但着丝粒却是基因组中进化最快的区域之一，即使在较短的进化时间尺度上也表现出广泛的变异。在此，我们旨在通过绘制138种芽殖酵母物种及超过2,500个自然菌株分离株的着丝粒进化图谱，来理解新型着丝粒如何出现并达到固定。我们表明，新着丝粒通过漂变及随后的选择逐步扩散，而相对缓慢进化的动粒界面决定了哪些新着丝粒变异体可被容忍。综合来看，我们的发现为塑造着丝粒进化的进化约束和轨迹提供了见解。
